lead: Rochester plumbing deals with lake-effect snow, deep cold, old homes and lead service lines. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Rochester.
risk: frozen pipes, lead service lines and aging pipes in older homes
risk_short: frozen pipes, lead lines and old pipes
why: The South Wedge, Corn Hill, Park Avenue and the 19th Ward have homes from the 1850s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines in many cases.
Long, snowy winters freeze pipes near exterior walls and in vacant homes. Almost every home has a basement with the water heater and floor drains.
water: Rochester's water comes mainly from Hemlock and Canadice lakes in the Finger Lakes. It is soft. The city has a program to replace lead service lines.
tips: Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Ask the Water Bureau about your service line material.
areas: PipeMend works in the South Wedge, Park Avenue, Corn Hill, the Neighborhood of the Arts, Highland Park, Maplewood and every other Rochester neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Rochester Bureau of Buildings and Zoning, which also oversees plumber licensing in the city. New York has no statewide plumber license.

faq.q: Where does Rochester's water come from?
faq.a: Mostly from Hemlock and Canadice lakes, two of the Finger Lakes, plus some Lake Ontario water bought from the county. The lake water is soft.
